answer.policy_title: Knee Arthroplasty - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin
criteria_quotes: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty using Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved devices is considered medically necessary for members with advanced osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee affecting only a single compartment (medial, lateral or patellofemoral).
Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint.
Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination.
Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament.
Patient’s knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less.
Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint.

History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record, with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy).

Conservative therapy includes all of the following, unless contraindicated: anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; activity modification; supervised physical therapy; assistive device use, required for persons with relative contraindications and optional for others; and therapeutic injections into the knee, required for persons with relative contraindications and optional for others.

Member has none of the following contraindications to unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: previous proximal tibial osteotomy or distal femoral osteotomy; tibial or femoral shaft deformity; radiographic evidence of medial or lateral subluxation; flexion contracture greater than 15 degrees; varus deformity greater than 15 degrees for medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty or valgus deformity greater than 20 degrees for lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty; inflammatory or crystalline arthropathy; or subchondral bone loss due to large subchondral cysts or extensive focal osteonecrosis.

Member has none of the following absolute contraindications to joint replacement: active infection of the joint or active systemic bacteremia that has not been totally eradicated; active skin infection or an open wound within the planned surgical site; corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty; vascular insufficiency, significant muscular atrophy, or neuromuscular disease severe enough to compromise implant stability or postoperative recovery; osseous abnormalities that cannot be optimally managed; or allergy to implant components.
For members with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty should be appropriately addressed in the medical record.
answer.appeal_deadline: 2027-02-03, as stated in the denial notice. This is 180 days from the 2026-08-07 notice date.
answer.submission_route: Aetna's public member instructions state that the member may appeal by calling Member Services at the telephone number on the member ID card or by mailing the appeal to the address on the EOB. Aetna also provides a Member appeal form. Include the denial notice/reference number POC-8EE886247D-14307, member name and ID, the disputed CPT code 27446, and clinical records or other supporting information. The denial notice supplied here does not provide a mailing address, so use the address on the EOB or obtain the correct address by calling the number on the ID card or denial letter.

Aetna's knee-arthroplasty precertification form specifically directs non-Medicare members to review Clinical Policy Bulletin #660. However, the denial letter also refers to clinical review criteria, and the exact version or any additional case-specific criteria applied to Morgan was not identified in the public materials retrieved. Call the number on the member ID card or denial letter and request: the exact policy version used for the 2026-08-07 determination; every clinical-review or utilization-review criterion applied to CPT 27446; the specific criterion or criteria not met; and the clinical reviewer's rationale and records considered. Aetna's member denial page states that Member Services can send documents needed for an appeal.
